guideposts.label: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 20 of the Tour de France 2026
guideposts.detail: L’Alpe d’Huez, second leg! And this one is even harder than stage 19, even though the riders won’t tackle the legendary 21-hairpin that crowned Tadej Pogacar on Friday. This time, they reach the resort via the Col de Sarenne ascent (12.8 km at 7.3%), whose summit is 14.4 kilometres from the line. Before that, they will pass Col de la Croix de Fer (HC), Col du Télégraphe (cat 1), and Col du Galibie

guideposts.label: Le Bourg d’Oisans, at the bottom of Alpe d’Huez
guideposts.detail: With its special location, Le Bourg d’Oisans first appeared on the map of the Tour de France on the back of the maiden Alpe d’Huez ascent, in 1952. Following his stage win and conquest of the Maillot Jaune, Fausto Coppi triumphed in Italy, as the race headed to Sestrières. Today marks the 26th stage start from the city. The last one, in 2022 (stage 13), smiled on Denmark: Mads Pedersen took his ma

guideposts.label: Saving France’s Tour?
guideposts.detail: At the start of stage 20, French riders are yet to win a stage. It has only happened twice in history, and these references are not good omens for local heroes: the Tours 1926 and 1999 are the only ones in history with no victory for France. Can this year’s contenders flip the script? At least, they’re coming closer and closer to the mark. Finishing 2nd yesterday at L’Alpe d’Huez, Lenny Martinez a

guideposts.label: Green jersey
guideposts.detail: Battling at the front and making the most of the intermediate sprint, Mads Pedersen (Lidl-Trek) pushed his lead back up to 57 points to Jasper Philipsen (Alpecin-Premier Tech): 502 points for the Dane, 445 for the Belgian sprinter. Biniam Girmay (NSN) is still third with 361 points. Today’s stage offers up to 45 points: 25 for the first rider at the intermediate sprint (Saint-Julien-Mont-Denis, km

guideposts.label: Team classification
guideposts.detail: Lidl-Trek still lead the overall team standings with a margin of 19’33’’ against UAE Emirates-XRG. Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe are in third place overall (+1h06’53’’).

guideposts.label: Combativity award
guideposts.detail: Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) races with a distinctive bib again as he was named the most combative rider yesterday. This is his seventh combativity award on the Tour. He took one in 2020, two in 2024, and four this year. Carapaz also won the Super Combativity award in 2024.

guideposts.label: An early visit to Vaujany
guideposts.detail: As they head to Col de la Croix de Fer early in the stage, the riders ride through the territory of Vaujany, whose station is connected to L’Alpe d’Huez. Several events have held stages here: Paris-Nice, Tour cycliste féminin, and, most recently, the Critérium du Dauphiné (now known as Tour Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes), in 2022. That year, stage 7 started in Saint-Chaffrey, passed the Col du Galibier and

guideposts.label: Stage 20 of the Tour de France 2026 is ON!
guideposts.detail: The 160-man peloton just passed km 0.

guideposts.label: Oliveira is the first attacker of the day
guideposts.detail: He is followed by Schmid, Abrahamsen, Dhondt, Velasco...

guideposts.label: 6 leaders at km 3
guideposts.detail: Georg Steinhauser (EF Education-EasyPost), Jonas Abrahamsen (Uno-X Mobility), Baptiste Veistroffer (Lotto Intermarché), Xabier Mikel Azparren (Pinarello Q36.5), Joris Delbove (Total Energies) and Warren Barguil (Picnic PostNL) are 15 seconds ahead of the bunch.

guideposts.label: A group of six riders attacked right from the start
A KOM festival
guideposts.detail: Three HC climbs and cat 1 ascent on the eve of the Parisian grand finale: the contenders for the polka-dot jersey have known for months that today is the big rendezvous with a whooping 70 KOM points up for grabs. On paper, that means eight riders can still edge Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost), all the way to Mauro Schmid (Jayco AlUla), who has 22 points. Mainly, the battle for the mountain

guideposts.label: Jorgenson attacks, Ayuso reacts
guideposts.detail: They're followed by Bernal, Carapaz, Castrillo...

guideposts.label: Healy sets off
guideposts.detail: He's followed by Armirail, one of the Johannessen twins, Foss, Riccitello...

guideposts.label: Barguil and Steinhauser push the pace
guideposts.detail: The duo are 20 seconds from the summit. Abrahamsen is right behind them. Counter-attackers are yet to make a difference. The gap is down to 35 seconds.

guideposts.label: 4 leaders again
guideposts.detail: Abrahamsen and Azparren are back with Barguil and Steinhauser. Meanwhile, the bunch explodes due to the pace set by Visma-Lease a Bike. Egan Bernal was just dropped after Ben O'Connor, Mauro Schmid, Nils Politt, Raul Garcia Pierna...

guideposts.label: Around 40 riders in the bunch
guideposts.detail: They are 20 seconds behind the four leaders, and they still have 16 kilometres left to reach Col de la Croix de Fer. Quinn Simmons (Lidl-Trek) reacts on a small downhill section.

guideposts.label: Ayuso is very active
guideposts.detail: The Spaniard lost his place in the GC top 5 yesterday. He is out for revenge.

guideposts.label: The attackers are caught because of Ayuso's acceleration
guideposts.detail: The Spanish climber insists 15 kilometres from the summit. He's followed by Healy, Hindley, Riccitello, Braz Afonso...

guideposts.label: A group of around fifteen riders has broken away from the peloton
A 15-man breakaway?
guideposts.detail: Ayuso forced the split and now Armirail sets the pace. Jorgenson and Kuss are in this group, as well as Carapaz and Paret-Peintre. Piganzoli sets off from the bunch paced by Yates.

guideposts.label: Not much of a margin for the attackers
guideposts.detail: Onto the last 7 kilometres of ascent, the gap drops down to 35 seconds.

guideposts.label: 29.7 kilometres in the first hour
guideposts.detail: They've gained aroung 1,400 metres of elevation.

guideposts.label: Carapaz attacks 3.7 km from the summit
guideposts.detail: Paret-Peintre tries to chase him.

guideposts.label: Richard Carapaz launched an attack at the front of the race
Ackermann abandons
guideposts.detail: 159 riders are still in the race.

guideposts.label: Pedersen attacks from the GC group
guideposts.detail: Carapaz is 2 km from the summit. +15'' Paret-Peintre +50'' Breakaway +1'30'' Pedersen +1'55'' Peloton

guideposts.label: Benoot attacks from the GC group (+2'15'')
guideposts.detail: Meanwhile, Carapaz is 20 seconds ahead of Paret-Peintre in the final kilometre of ascent.

guideposts.label: Mads Pedersen breaks away from the Yellow Jersey group
Benoot has crashed on the downhill
guideposts.detail: He rapidly gets back up on his feet. The GC group ride past him while he fiwes his handlebar.

guideposts.label: The gaps at the summit
guideposts.detail: +20’’ V. Paret-Peintre +1’ Breakaway +1’30’’ Pedersen +1’50’’ Benoot +2’10’’ Peloton

guideposts.label: Paret-Peintre joins Carapaz at the front
guideposts.detail: They slow down. The Ayuso group trails by 1 minute. Pedersen is right behind them.

guideposts.label: 15 leaders: Ayuso, Carapaz, Pedersen, Kuss...
guideposts.detail: The chasers catch the two leaders at km 48.

guideposts.label: Van Wilder has abandoned
guideposts.detail: Ilan Van Wilder (Soudal Quick-Step) is out of the race after a crash.

guideposts.label: Bruno Armirail (Visma I Lease a Bike)
Soon in Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne
guideposts.detail: Home to today's intermediate sprint, at the heart of the Maurienne valley, the town is surrounded by Alpine summits and has thus often been visited by races such as the Tour de France, the Critérium du Dauphiné, the Tour de l’Avenir, the Tour des Pays de Savoie… Romain Bardet is the last winner in Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne, after a 35-km solo attack to claim stage 18 of the Tour de France 2015. Toda

guideposts.label: Into the final 100 kilometres
guideposts.detail: Jorgenson and Armirail (Visma-Lease a Bike) take strong turns to push the gap up to 3 minutes.

guideposts.label: Armirail is done...
guideposts.detail: Piganzoli and Foss take over the pace-setting. Paret-Peintre hangs on but he struggles.

guideposts.label: Paret-Peintre is dropped for real
guideposts.detail: The French climber doesn't surrender but the gap opens: 15 seconds with 8 kilometres left to Col du Télégraphe.

guideposts.label: 10 riders at the front
guideposts.detail: Foss and Piganzoli still take turns. Braz Afonso is dropped.

guideposts.label: At the front in the Alpine passes
Halfway through the stage
guideposts.detail: The leaders are less than two kilometres from Col du Télégraphe. The gap to the GC group is decreasing: 4'20''.

guideposts.label: Headed for the highest summit of the Tour
guideposts.detail: The riders just passed by Valloire, where Tadej Pogacar won stage 4 of the Tour de France 2024.

guideposts.label: Souvenir Henri Desgrange
guideposts.detail: The Souvenir Henri Desgrange was created in 1947 to celebrate the legacy of the race founder, who passed away in 1940. The 1947 edition was the first without him, marking the race’s return after World War II. Initially, the award was not related to a climb: the first Souvenir Henri Desgrange was given near his last home, “Villa Mia” in Beauvallon. In 1949, a monument honoring Desgrange was built n

guideposts.label: The gap is on the rise again
guideposts.detail: With Healy pulling the breakaway and UAE Emirates XRG back at the front of the bunch, the gap increases to 4'15''. Another sign that Healy is going strong: Johannessen has just been dropped, 9 kilometres from the summit.

guideposts.label: High altitude battles
guideposts.detail: The attackers are now riding more than 2,000 metres above sea level. Healy is spent. Carapaz takes over... And Johannessen returns. The gap to the peloton is up to 4'30''.

guideposts.label: Carapaz attacks 5 kilometres from the summit
guideposts.detail: The breakaway explodes. Kuss, Hindley and Riccitello are the strongest behind him. Ayuso tries to get back to them.

guideposts.label: 4 leaders on Col du Galibier
guideposts.detail: Kuss and Hindley worked together to close the gap to Carapaz 3 kilometres from the summit. Riccitello managed to follow them.

guideposts.label: Richard Carapaz is caught by three of his breakaway
Last kilometre of ascent for the 4 leaders
guideposts.detail: Ayuso trails by 15 seconds. And the peloton by 5'30''.

guideposts.label: Carapaz polka-dot jersey on the Galibier: it was meant to be
guideposts.detail: Carapaz has a lead of 42 points at the top of the KOM standings, while 24 remain available across today and tomorrow's stage. When Richard Carapaz went to Europe in 2016, he joined a cycling club called Asociación Deportiva Galibier, which at that time competed under the name Equipo Lizarte and is now known as Equipo Finisher, the feeder team of Equipo Kern Pharma. The club’s name came from the ad

guideposts.label: Into the final 50 kilometres
guideposts.detail: Carapaz, Ayuso, Hindley and Kuss lead the way on the downhil. Riccitello trails by 15 seconds after a bit of a scare. Pogacar drives the GC group with a gap of 4'30''. A handful of stragglers, including Skjelmose, are a handful of seconds behind.

guideposts.label: The second back-to-back at Alpe d’Huez
guideposts.detail: L’Alpe d’Huez hosts a finish for the 33rd time, the day after Tadej Pogacar became the 25th different rider to win here. This is the second time in history two stages finish at L’Alpe d’Huez in the same edition. When the route of the 1979 edition was presented in October 1978, L’Alpe d’Huez was only supposed to host one stage finish, on day 17, and the following finish was set at Vars, who withdre

guideposts.label: 30 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: Kuss, Hindley, Ayuso and Carapaz are back on the valley, ahead of the final categorised climb of the day. Riccitello trails by 40 seconds. Pogacar pulls the GC group with a gap of 3'50''. He is followed, in that order, by Prodhomme, Seixas, Del Toro, Evenepoel, Van Gils, Skjelmose, Arensman, T. Johannessen, and Martinez.

guideposts.label: The final giant of the Tour 2026: Col de Sarenne
guideposts.detail: This climb (12.8 km at 7.3%) is a new addition to the Tour de France. In 2013, the route passed over this summit, albeit in the opposite direction: the climb began at Alpe d’Huez and the descent led towards Mizoën (km 144.4), a village at the foot of this side of the pass. In 2017, this climb was featured in the Critérium du Dauphiné, on a stage finishing at Alpe d’Huez and won by the British ride

guideposts.label: First accelerations in the breakaway
guideposts.detail: Kuss and Hindley test their rivals. Carapaz and Ayuso react.

guideposts.label: Ayuso is distanced, Carapaz struggles
guideposts.detail: Hindley and Kuss collaborate 10 kilometres from the summit.

guideposts.label: Change to the route of the final stage
guideposts.detail: As numerous wildfires are currently affecting France, particularly the Gironde region, emergency services are fully mobilized to combat the blazes, while internal security forces are working to secure the affected areas and protect the population. In light of this, the Ministry of Interior has decided to redeploy a portion of the internal security forces initially mobilized to ensure security for

guideposts.label: It’s now Nicolas Prodhomme leading the Yellow Jersey group
Hindley and Carapaz catch Kuss
guideposts.detail: They are 5 kilometres from the summit. Meanwhile, Decathlon CMA CGM accelerate in the GC group. Prodhomme sets the pace, followed by Riccitello, Seixas... and then Del Toro, Evenepoel, Pogacar, Martinez, Skjelmose and T. Johannessen.

guideposts.label: Kuss attacks again
guideposts.detail: Carapaz and Hindley try to react. 3 kilometres to the summit. The G group trail by 1'50''.

guideposts.label: Carapaz vs Kuss
guideposts.detail: With 2 kilometres left on the ascent, Carapaz is 5 seconds behind Kuss, while the gap to Hindley is up to 30 seconds. +1'50'' Pogacar sets the pace with Del Toro, Evenepoel and Martinez on his wheel. They catch Ayuso.

guideposts.label: Kuss to end the USA's drought in the Tour?
guideposts.detail: It's been 5 years since a USA rider won a Tour de France stage. The last one to do so was none other than Sepp Kuss, in Andorra la Vella in 2021.

guideposts.label: Kusshas has crashed 7 kilometres from the line
guideposts.detail: He rapidly got back up o nhis bike. Carapaz trails by around 15 seconds.

guideposts.label: Kuss crashes again with 6 km remaining
guideposts.detail: Carapaz passes him.

guideposts.label: Evenepoel attacks with 3 km to go
guideposts.detail: Del Toro loses a few metres. Pogacar tries to help him.

guideposts.label: Richard Carapaz wins stage 20 of the Tour de France 2026!
guideposts.detail: His third stage win at the Tour (the second this year), and his 10th in Grand Tours.

guideposts.label: Pogacar and Del Toro complete the top 5 arm in arm
guideposts.detail: 1. Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) 2. Remco Evenepoel (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), +26'' 3. Sepp Kuss (Visma-Lease a Bike), +31'' 4. Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG), +1'05'' 5. Isaac del Toro (UAE Emirates XRG), +1'05''
